title: response_mock plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `response_mock` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component ResponseMockConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

ResponseMockConfig.description: Plugin: response_mock — Returns mock responses for API testing before backends are ready. Rule paths are relative to a prefix listen_path with trailing slashes trimmed before stripping; exact (`=`), regex (`~`), root (`/`), and host-only scopes match the full request path. Rules are evaluated in order (first match wins); an optional per-rule `match` adds exact request header / query parameter conditions. Supports HTTP and WebSocket upgrade handshakes only: a match short-circuits only the HTTP handshake response and does not establish or mock an upgraded WebSocket frame stream, so a 2xx rule that matches a WebSocket handshake fails closed with 500 on every frontend (H1/H2/H3). Native gRPC (`application/grpc` on H2/H3) is unsupported — the plugin is not selected for that protocol because Reject results normalize to trailers-only gRPC errors that discard configured bodies. Unknown top-level and per-rule keys are rejected. The free-form headers map accepts string-valued response headers but rejects protocol-managed hop-by-hop and framing names (`Connection`, `Keep-Alive`, `Proxy-Authenticate`, `Proxy-Connection`, `TE`, `Trailer`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Upgrade`, `Content-Length`, including case variants); the gateway derives Content-Length from the mock body/status/method and strips connection/framing fields at the final H1/H2/H3 response boundary. Status codes must be final (200–599); informational statuses, including 101, are rejected. `delay_ms` runs under the shared fault-delay bounds (one-minute ceiling, FERRUM_MAX_CONCURRENT_FAULT_DELAYS budget, shutdown and HTTP/3 peer cancellation). HEAD omits content bytes while keeping representation Content-Length; 204/205/304 omit body and Content-Length on every frontend (H1/H2/H3). Runtime construction and request-flavor enforcement are the authoritative final boundaries. Size limits apply independently per rule and field; there is no aggregate instance memory budget. For example, 1024 rules can retain 256 MiB of body payload alone, plus headers, conditions, regexes, and other overhead. Runtime string limits count UTF-8 bytes; maxLength counts Unicode characters and is only a coarse schema guard.

rules.description: Mock rules evaluated in order (first match wins)

method.description: HTTP method token to match (omit or null to match all methods). When supplied it must be a non-empty HTTP method token (runtime validates via http::Method). Registered standard methods are matched case-insensitively (get matches GET); extension methods are case-sensitive per RFC 9110 section 9.1 and match the configured spelling exactly.

path.description: Non-empty rule path. Relative to a prefix listen_path (e.g., /users for listen_path /api/v1). For exact (`=`), regex (`~`), root (`/`), and host-only proxies, use the full request path. Regex rule paths use a ~ prefix (auto-anchored). Full Rust regex compilation remains a runtime-only check.

match.description: Optional extra request conditions; every listed condition must hold. A rule whose conditions do not hold is skipped and evaluation continues with the next rule. Omitted or null adds no conditions.

additionalProperties.description: At most 8192 UTF-8 bytes at runtime. maxLength counts Unicode characters and is only a coarse schema guard; runtime byte validation is authoritative.

headers.description: 1–16 header name → exact value pairs. Matches when every named header is present on the client-sent request with a field line byte-for-byte equal to the value (names case-insensitive and unique ignoring case, values case-sensitive). Gateway-asserted names (`x-consumer-*`, the private GeoIP header, path-param headers) are rejected. Values must be valid HTTP header values of at most 8192 bytes and are redacted in non-admin config projections. Reads pristine client field lines, so earlier header additions, rewrites, and removals do not affect matching.

propertyNames.description: 1–256 UTF-8 bytes at runtime. maxLength counts Unicode characters and is only a coarse schema guard; runtime byte validation is authoritative.

additionalProperties.description: At most 8192 UTF-8 bytes at runtime. maxLength counts Unicode characters and is only a coarse schema guard; runtime byte validation is authoritative.

query_params.description: 1–16 query parameter name → exact value pairs, compared against the current percent-decoded query map (last occurrence wins; a bare `?flag` has the value ""). Unlike match.headers, earlier query additions, rewrites, and removals affect matching. At default priorities, request_transformer (3000) runs before response_mock (3030); priority overrides can change which rewrites have run at evaluation. Names are 1–256 UTF-8 bytes, values at most 8192 UTF-8 bytes. Values are redacted in non-admin config projections.

status_code.description: HTTP status code to return (default 200). Must be a final status 200–599. Informational statuses (100–199, including 101) and values outside 100–599 are rejected at construction rather than coerced: a mock never upgrades the connection, and HTTP/2 / HTTP/3 cannot carry 101. A 2xx rule that matches a WebSocket handshake fails closed with status 500 on every frontend instead of claiming an established WebSocket. Omitted or null selects 200.

headers.description: Response headers (default content-type application/json), at most 64 entries with values of at most 8192 bytes. Omitted or null selects that default. Names must be HTTP field-name tokens. Protocol-managed hop-by-hop and framing names (`connection`, `content-length`, `keep-alive`, `proxy-authenticate`, `proxy-connection`, `te`, `trailer`, `transfer-encoding`, `upgrade`) are rejected at construction, including case variants. Values must be valid HTTP header values (HTAB and printable ASCII).

body.description: Response body string (default empty), at most 262144 UTF-8 bytes at runtime. maxLength counts Unicode characters and is only a coarse schema guard; runtime byte validation is authoritative, so a multibyte body can be refused below maxLength. Omitted or null selects empty. On the wire, HEAD responses omit content bytes while keeping representation Content-Length. Statuses 204, 205, and 304 omit both the body and Content-Length even when this field is non-empty. Shared synthetic-response finalization keeps H1, H2, and H3 aligned.

delay_ms.description: Simulated latency in milliseconds (default 0). Omitted or null selects 0. Must be an unsigned integer 0–60000 (1 minute, the shared fault-delay ceiling); negative values and values above the cap are rejected at config validation. The delay counts against the process-wide FERRUM_MAX_CONCURRENT_FAULT_DELAYS budget (shared with fault_injection): an exhausted budget or gateway shutdown serves the mock immediately, and a client that is gone (HTTP/3 connection close) ends the delay with 499. A non-completing delay records `fault_delay_outcome`.

passthrough_on_no_match.description: If true, unmatched requests (including WebSocket upgrades) continue to the backend. If false (default), returns 404. Omitted or null selects false.
